messages:
Alex: FYI noticed a sharp p99 spike on the hosted GPU fleet around 00:20 UTC. Saw a 2-3x tail regression for several small-decode models.
Lin: Ugh. Any traces or batching logs to point to a culprit?
Alex: Pulled traces + batching debug. Short take: a wave of KV-cache hits confused the packer. Hit requests still carried full prompt length in the packing estimator, so mixed hit+cold batches inflated virtual seq_len and triggered the long/slow kernel path.
Maria: That's surprising — hits should reduce work. How did we end up with long-seq kernels?
Alex: Because the packer uses reported prompt_len + decode_len to decide packing and kernel selection. If hits aren't accounted for, reported length looks big even though compute is tiny. The packer then aggregates with cold requests and we exceed the kernel threshold.
Ben: Numbers? p50/p95/p99 and batch stats would help.
Alex: From 2022-08-17 00:15 run (trimmed):
```
p50=9ms, p95=38ms, p99=245ms
avg batch_size=13, avg microbatch=3
kv_hit_ratio ~= 58%
avg reported_seq_len = 192
avg actual decode tokens (post-cache) = 4
```
Lin: So packer thought ~192 seq but actual compute tiny. Kernsel switched because virtual length > short-kernel threshold.
Sara: Two routes: (A) make packer compute an effective_seq for kv-hit items (small constant), or (B) isolate high-kv traffic into a separate fastpath queue that never uses long kernels.
Jon: Fastpath queue is cleaner for isolation, but more moving pieces. Effective_seq is conservative and quick.
Alex: I ran a small experiment (A/B across 4 nodes) with effective_seq clamp: kv_effective_len = min(6, prompt_len). Also enabled kv_hit_priority admission. Outcome: p99 on experiment nodes dropped from 245ms to ~82ms, batcher chose short kernels for ~90% of microbatches. Cold-only latency rose ~4-6ms p95.
Ben: Any cost implications? Smaller batches usually reduce throughput.
Alex: Throughput per-GPU slightly down but unit cost per decode token improved (we avoided expensive long-kernel inefficiencies). Tail SLA improved which is the main customer metric.
Maria: Need fairness safeguards. We shouldn't starve cold traffic on multi-tenant hosts.
Alex: Agreed. Proposed conservative defaults in patch:
```yaml
batcher:
  kv_hit_effective_len: 6  # treat KV hits as short sequences for packing decision
  kv_fastpath_admit_fraction: 0.12  # fraction of admission budget reserved for kv fastpath
  kv_apply_threshold: 0.5  # only apply fastpath when pending-kv fraction > 50%
  fastpath_queue_limit: 40
```
deploy-bot: CI: batching-config-tests passed (tests/batcher/test_kv_effective_len.py)
Lin: Also update kernel selection to use median(effective_seq) across microbatches, not raw reported values. Otherwise kernsel still misclassifies some batches.
Sara: Add telemetry fields: batch.kv_fraction, batch.effective_seq_median, batch.selected_kernel, batch.kv_fastpath_applied. Make an alert if p99 spikes or if kv_fastpath_applied correlates with worse cold-tail.
Jon: Rollout plan suggestion: config-only rollout to 10% traffic for 48h -> measure fairness and tail -> then enable kernsel change behind feature-flag on 5 canaries for 24h -> wider.
Ben: I'll run synthetic fairness benchmarks (mixed hot/cold tenants) and long-run soak.
Maria: Also document limitations: client-supplied prompt metadata can be wrong (masking, client-side trimming). Add SDK note and server-side sanity checks (clamp effective_len).
Alex: Action items: open PR for config+tests (I'll do PR #3672), Lin will add telemetry and dashboards, Ben runs fairness tests, Sara drafts safe canary and rollback runbook, Jon adds feature-flag for kernsel. I'll attach traces + flamegraphs to /mnt/ci/perf/2119876543/ for review.
Lin: Nice. One more thought: consider admission token-budget targets rather than pure fraction so heavy token requests don't overcommit fastpath.
Alex: Good call. We can cap fastpath by token budget and by request count. Will add to PR.
Sara: Thanks all. Let's watch the 10% canary closely and be ready to revert.
Alex: I'll post canary metrics update here when available.
Lin: :thumbsup:
